action_sequence_note: VERIFIED (self-run gate, reached_level=3, reproduced=True): 42-label banked L1-L2 prefix (from results/arc_loop_solve_lf52.json solution_labels) + 104 labels of live L3 play. The live labels include an exploratory first attempt that ended in a stranded board and an in-game auto-reset (triggered mid-stream by a click on the keyhole structure), followed by the clean winning line -- the full stream replays deterministically as gated.
novel_mechanics_found: lf52 L3+ is multi-screen rail-carrier PEG SOLITAIRE with a built-in move oracle: ACTION6 on a peg paints a color-3 selection ring plus color-2 markers on every LEGAL landing square (pegs with no legal moves give a completely silent click) -- the game enumerates its own moves, eliminating guesswork. Jumps are two-cell hops over an adjacent peg (crossed peg removed). Carriers (bccccb sprites) are mobile sockets on rails driven by ACTION1-4, and ALL carriers move simultaneously on each press (each in whatever direction it can); a peg jumps INTO an aligned carrier socket over a crossed peg, rides it across rooms/screens (camera follows), and jumps out the same way -- the L2 registry mechanic generalized to a network of rails, shafts, and inverted-U ducts. The world is larger than one screen and scrolls. L4 introduces TORCHES (color-15 boxes with color-7 cores): crossable-but-indestructible jump obstacles that let a SOLO peg travel (hop over a torch, torch survives) -- breaking the classic solitaire rule that lone pegs are stuck. Stranding detection: if no legal moves remain with >1 peg, all pegs recolor (fill 14 -> 2) and the board auto-resets to the level start (unlimited retries, no timer). The win condition is global reduce-to-ONE-peg.
narrative: Resolved the 42-label verified prefix from the registry loop artifact (the generic resolver returned empty) and confirmed level 2. Discovered the selection-ring/landing-preview oracle on the first probe clicks, learned the jump grammar, and walked a 6-jump chain -- then stranded the board (4 mutually unreachable survivors) and learned the auto-reset mechanic the hard way. Second attempt: full-map survey first (rail networks, two carriers including an inverted-U duct linking the west and east screens), then a planned 9-jump global line: drain the west rooms into a single rail-carried peg, clear all seven east pegs with a column cascade ending in a carrier-loading jump, ride the U-duct back west, and kill the isolated bottom-left pair from the carrier -- reduced to one peg and levels_completed hit 3. Self-ran the reproduction gate (146 labels, reached_level=3, reproduced=True). Continued into L4: solved its first three phases live (torch-hop chain across the entrance hall, carrier relay, east-wing vertical torch-ladder cascade and a two-peg merge into a third carrier) before reaching a dense central hub with at least two more pegs, a fourth carrier, and multi-screen geometry that needs systematic re-mapping; stopped there with ~160 steps left rather than risk a stranding reset that would burn the remaining budget -- L4 is clearly solvable with the documented mechanics and a fresh budget.
gotchas: ACTION6 on a peg = select + paint legal landings in color 2; a peg with NO legal moves gives a totally silent click (ndiff=1, just the move counter) -- use this as a free move-enumerator.
All carriers move SIMULTANEOUSLY on ACTION1-4 (each in whatever direction its rail allows); track every carrier position when planning alignment.
Carriers are mobile sockets: jump in over a crossed peg when aligned, ride, jump out; an empty aligned carrier socket previews as a legal landing.
Torches (color-15/7) are crossable, indestructible jump obstacles -- a solo peg CAN travel via torch-hops; torch positions are the intended highways.

Stranding >1 peg with no moves recolors pegs 14->2 and auto-resets the level (no timer, unlimited retries); plan reduce-to-1 globally before jumping -- greedy local merges strand isolated pairs (e.g. two pegs separated by one empty socket can never interact unaided).
The top pixel row is a two-tone move counter (cosmetic).
The world scrolls: camera follows carrier moves and peg selections near edges; ALL click coordinates are VIEW-relative -- re-verify positions after any scroll.
Clicking the keyhole-shaped ffff structure (L3 bottom-left) reset the board.
The 42-label banked prefix is in results/arc_loop_solve_lf52.json under solution_labels (the exp4460 generic resolver returns empty for lf52).
